rationale: ROUND 2. Round 1 returned REVISE and the gating objection was CORRECT, so this round is a real widening, not a defence. bug_historian (HIGH) and guardian (HIGH) both said the landmine 'There are THREE pages upsert helpers and they have OPPOSITE collision policies' names siblings the patch never touched, and that fixing one call site of a shared judgement while its siblings stay unfixed is 016b §9's recurring shape. I checked. THEY WERE RIGHT: three more unguarded `meta_description = EXCLUDED.meta_description` clauses existed, each with the same empty-default upstream — apply_adoption_plan_action.go:546 (bare type assertion yields ""), adopt_verbatim.go:470 (extractHTMLMetaDescription RETURNS "" when the source HTML has no meta tag, which makes it the likeliest of the three to fire, because re-adopting such a page blanks a good description), and cmd/webdesignport/import.go:182. All four are now guarded; a tree-wide sweep returns 0 unguarded and 4 guarded. THE OTHER OBJECTIONS, ANSWERED WITH EVIDENCE RATHER THAN ASSERTION. (a) UpsertPageForRole is safe BY CONSTRUCTION and it is ENUMERATED, not asserted: it rewrites only columns the caller names in `Refresh`, and all five live callers name url/title/sections or {} — none names meta_description. (b) Sibling columns in the same clause (bug_historian, medium): meta_description was the ONLY column in upsertPage's clause with an EMPTY default — name defaults to page-N, title to name, url is computed, page_type to "content", nav_label to title AND is already guarded. That asymmetry is precisely why this column and no other produced the defect. (c) 103's status (bug_historian, medium): it IS closed — bugs_closed/103_HANDOFF_2026-07-27_tool_pages_publish_their_build_brief_as_the_meta_description.md, checked at the path, not at an index. The objection's premise that the index lists it as OPEN is mistaken. (d) Prior art (tooling_provenance): the objection was fair and I had not looked. There ARE doc_notes landmines keyed pages.meta_description from 08-14, 08-15 and 08-18, and the idea_uk lane recorded the mechanism on 2026-08-15 in its own migration comment — 'pages is a materialised cache; site_db_actions.go:1173 re-upserts meta_description unconditionally, so a fix to pages alone regresses on the next plan sync' — four days before I filed 320. I should have grepped LANDMINES for the column before starting. That same cache/source split also VERIFIES migration 485 end to end, which was round 1's first reviewer check: write_site_plan_action.go:535 reads GetStringField(raw,"meta_description","") — exactly the key 485 now asks the planner for — and inserts it into site_plan_pages at :631, from which upsertPage binds it into pages. (e) Dead code (editquality/guardian, low): the driver now EXISTS — migration 486 seeds a meta-description-backfiller agent whose loop calls the action. It is deliberately HELD (filename suffix _HOLD, so the runner's SIDECAR_RE excludes it from --apply) because the live chassis is v1.0.1314 / d3590ca4 and merge-base --is-ancestor is FALSE with 145 commits unshipped: image first, then seeds. (f) Whitespace-only descriptions (editquality, low): the new ACTION already TrimSpace-es its candidate and refuses an empty result, so the write path cannot produce one; the upsert guard matches the nav_label precedent exactly, as the objection itself notes. bugs_open/320. `pages.meta_description` is the sentence Google prints under a page's title, and on this estate it is also the excerpt the blog-listing component renders in each card. MEASURED 2026-08-19: 407 of 731 active pages (55.7%) across 26 of 27 sites have none; three sites are at 100% (loancalculator.co.uk 43/43, adversecreditmortgage.co.uk 19/19, loanzy.uk 13/13). Two independent mechanisms, both still live. M1 (born empty): build-site-planner's `Return JSON:` page object asks for name/title/page_type/nav_label/nav_order/in_header/in_footer/sections and NOTHING else, while upsertPage reads `GetStringField(page,"meta_description","")` — it asks the plan for a key the plan was never told to produce. M2 (blanked later): the same upsert's ON CONFLICT sets `meta_description = EXCLUDED.meta_description` UNGUARDED, three lines below a nav_label clause that IS `COALESCE(NULLIF(...))`-guarded; combined with the "" default, any pass that omits the key overwrites a real description with a blank. M2 is PROVEN to have fired, not merely representable: site_snapshots.pages_snapshot carries the column, and four robot-hands.com pages holding 97/120/169/329 chars on 2026-04-10 read 0 today, all built_from_plan_version IS NOT NULL. Nothing repaired either: all seven writers of the column are create-or-upsert, `default_config ~* 'update[[:space:]]+pages'` over live agents returns 0 rows, and 0 of the 58 discovery_checks name the column. The route that LOOKED like a repair is the expensive one — two `content_rewrite` items filed against missing meta descriptions COMPLETED and wrote nothing (ec701bb3-85e7-40e7-bff1-2ce1ae104861, 13522562-2392-4db9-96b5-204ab67cb999; both targets still 0 chars, and the first page's own updated_at is AFTER the item closed). The cause is ownership: llm_fields/llm_field_specs are per-SECTION and this is a `pages` column, so no writer prompt can reach it. The owner reviewed the options on 2026-08-19 and chose the full fix (guard + planner field + a backfill producer). This submission is the Go half. The diagnosis loop run 7375631a-dfa1-4145-9a07-d13586f1a7cf returned UNVERIFIABLE on its iteration cap — cited as a contributor that supplied M2 and named the site_snapshots test, NOT as ratification; every figure above is first-hand.

edits.rationale: M2's fix. `meta_description = EXCLUDED.meta_description` becomes `COALESCE(NULLIF(EXCLUDED.meta_description, ''), pages.meta_description)`, matching the nav_label clause three lines above. A non-blank incoming value still wins, so a plan that DOES supply a description continues to update the page; only the destructive direction closes. This makes 'a replan silently destroys published copy' unrepresentable rather than merely unlikely.

Its upstream is `metaDesc, _ := pm["meta_description"].(string)` — a bare type assertion, so an adoption plan that omits the key (or carries a non-string) yields "" and the unguarded clause wrote that over a real description.

edits.rationale: ROUND 2, and the likeliest of the three to have fired. `extractHTMLMetaDescription` explicitly `return ""` when the source HTML carries no meta tag, so re-adopting a page whose source lacks a description blanked whatever the page already had.

ROUND 2. `p.MetaDescription` is "" for an imported page carrying none, so a re-import blanked an existing description. Included for completeness even though it is a CLI tool rather than the chassis: the landmine names it as one of the three helpers, and leaving it is exactly the one-of-N shape the objection is about.

The missing persist half. Takes a page id (or site_id+page_name, resolved in the same order as UpdatePageStatusAction so authors do not learn a second convention) plus a text field, and writes the column. New authority on a shared seam ships opt-in with the UNSAFE side OFF (owner ruling 2026-08-02 §2): `overwrite_existing` defaults to FALSE, so by default it fills a blank and refuses a page that already has copy. The policy lives in the UPDATE's own WHERE clause rather than a read-then-write, so it cannot race a concurrent writer. It REUSES datahelpers.MetaDescriptionLooksInternal — the bugs_closed/103 guard, whose own doc comment says it is exported so 'a discovery check or a backfill' can ask the same question — rather than re-deriving the brief-vs-public rule. Critically, the result map always distinguishes a write from a refusal with a named reason (empty_candidate / candidate_looks_internal / candidate_too_long / already_has_description), because a successful no-op is the exact failure this action exists to end; a missing DB connection is an ERROR, not a soft {"updated": false}, for the same reason.
edits.sketch:
const q = `
  UPDATE pages
  SET meta_description = $2, updated_at = NOW()
  WHERE id = $1
    AND ($3::bool OR COALESCE(meta_description, '') = '')
  RETURNING id`

err = params.DB.QueryRowContext(ctx, q, pageID, candidate, overwrite).Scan(&updatedID)
switch {
case err == sql.ErrNoRows:
    return map[string]interface{}{"updated": false, "reason": "already_has_description", ...}, nil
case err != nil:
    return nil, fmt.Errorf(...)
}

Each test is chosen to fail against a NAMED wrong implementation, and every mutation was actually RUN rather than asserted. Flip the overwrite_existing default to true -> 2 fail. Delete the MetaDescriptionLooksInternal branch -> 1 fails. Delete the guarded WHERE clause -> 3 fail. Restore -> green. NOTE A CORRECTION WORTH THE COUNCIL'S ATTENTION: the first version matched `regexp.QuoteMeta("UPDATE pages")` and its comment CLAIMED deleting the guard clause would kill it. Running the mutation showed it did not — with the clause gone the action still passed three args, WithArgs still matched, and all five stayed green. The expectation now matches the clause itself. That is the a-mutation-that-passes-may-have-hit-a-guard-in-series trap, caught only because the mutation was executed.

The whole actions package passed BOTH before and after the M2 fix — the behaviour was entirely untested, so nothing would have objected if a later edit reverted it. Asserts the SQL shape (local precedent: record_vision_finding_action_test.go:118) and pins the empty-string binding too, so the fix cannot be misread as 'the empty default was removed'. It was not; the default is still "", and that is now safe precisely BECAUSE the SQL refuses to write it over a value. Mutation verified: restoring `meta_description = EXCLUDED.meta_description` fails the first test.

plan.risks: ROUND 2 ADDITIONS. The three new edits widen the change from one write path to four, so the blast radius is now every page-creation path on the estate rather than only the plan-driven one. Each is the same one-clause, strictly NARROWING edit: it can only preserve a value the old clause would have destroyed, and a non-blank incoming value still wins everywhere. The behaviour a caller loses is the ability to blank a description by passing "", and no caller does that deliberately — in all four the "" arises from an omitted key, an absent meta tag, or a failed type assertion. adopt_verbatim and webdesignport/import are ADOPTION paths, where a re-adopt genuinely might be intended to resync a page to its source; if a source page has had its description deliberately REMOVED, the adopted copy now keeps the old one instead of following the source. That is the one real behaviour change in this round and it is stated rather than buried — it is the right trade against silently blanking published copy, but a reviewer should weigh it. BLAST RADIUS OF THE UPSERT EDIT, MEASURED NOT ASSUMED: upsertPage is the plan-driven page writer, so the clause is on the path of every plan-built page — 515 of 731 active pages are built_from_plan_version IS NOT NULL. The change is strictly narrowing: it can only PRESERVE a value that the old clause would have destroyed. A caller that intends to blank a description deliberately can no longer do so through this path; no such caller exists today (the only producer of a blank is an omitted key), but that is the behaviour change a reviewer should weigh. The new action is UNEXERCISED IN PRODUCTION. It is registered but nothing calls it until a workflow is seeded, so its deployment contract (DB handle present, page id resolvable from the shapes a real loop emits) is unverified by anything except tests. Registered as SEO-004 with 'built, not yet exercised' rather than 'deployed', deliberately. The action can write public copy. That authority is bounded three ways: overwrite_existing defaults false so existing copy is never replaced silently; MetaDescriptionLooksInternal refuses brief-shaped text (the bugs_closed/103 failure); and a 320-character ceiling shared with datahelpers rather than a second number. What it does NOT bound is quality of the LLM sentence — that is the calling workflow's prompt, submitted separately. Migration 485 (build-site-planner asks for a description) is ALREADY LIVE from 2026-08-19, config being live on apply. It is safe ahead of this Go half: a non-blank incoming value has always won the old clause too, and 485 only makes incoming values non-blank. Stated rather than left for a reviewer to work out. 112 of the 407 empty pages are NOT plan-managed, so no replan reaches them. They are the population the new action exists for, and they remain empty until a workflow drives it. Flagged so 'the fix shipped' is not read as 'the 407 are filled'.
